consent.title: The doctor is asking permission to record the visit.
consent.lead: The recording lets the doctor look at you instead of the screen, without breaking off to fill in your chart. Declining changes nothing: the visit goes ahead as usual.

facts.audioText: Speech is transcribed as it goes; the sound itself is never written to disk. Only text remains in the chart.
facts.ownMicTerm: Only your own microphone is recorded.
facts.ownMicText: The doctor records themselves, you record yourself. There is no shared track.
facts.stopTerm: You can stop at any moment.
facts.stopText: A “Stop” button stays visible the whole time, and what you said is deleted — not merely no longer recorded, but deleted.
facts.beforeTerm: Until you answer, nothing is recorded
facts.beforeText: — neither your voice nor the doctor's.
facts.cardTerm: The text goes into your chart and nowhere else.
facts.cardText: It becomes a draft of the visit; the doctor checks it, edits it and signs it personally. The system signs nothing on the doctor's behalf.

consent.tip: If you can, put on headphones: from speakers the doctor's voice reaches your recording and is written down as your words.

patient.revoked: Recording stopped, what you said has been deleted
patient.mobile: Recording a visit from a phone is not possible — only from a computer. This conversation is not being recorded.

doctor.mobile: Visits can only be recorded from a computer: on a phone the microphone is taken by the call.
doctor.waiting: Waiting for the patient's consent. Nothing is recorded until they answer.
doctor.peerMobile: The patient joined from a phone — recording will not work: the microphone there is taken by the call. You will have to fill in the chart as usual.
doctor.declined: The patient declined the recording — fill in the chart as usual
doctor.revoked: The patient stopped the recording. A draft can still be assembled from what was said before that.

how.summary: How to get a clear recording
how.headphonesText: Echo cancellation is switched off in the recording on purpose — it clips quiet speech, which is the hardest thing to reconstruct from memory afterwards. The trade-off: from speakers the patient's voice reaches your microphone, and in the transcript their words are attributed to you. “I think I have pneumonia” from a patient is a complaint; from a doctor it is a diagnosis.
how.micTerm: Choose the microphone here, not only in the call.
how.micText: The recording runs as a separate stream: if the external microphone is selected only in the call settings, the system one will still be recorded.
how.distanceText: A headset five centimetres from the mouth is clearer than an expensive microphone two metres away. Keep it 15–25 cm away and slightly off the direct breath. A bare, echoing room hurts more than steady background noise.
how.ownMicText: Only your own microphone is recorded: the patient records themselves. Recording starts only after their consent, and they can stop it at any moment — then what they said is deleted.

draft.title: Visit draft
draft.lead: Assembled from the conversation. Check and correct it — whatever stays in the fields goes into the chart. The entry is saved as a draft; signing is a separate action.
draft.otherTitle: Said, but not sorted into sections:
draft.otherHint: Move whatever belongs to the visit into the right fields. We did not guess the section: putting it in the wrong one is worse than leaving the choice to the doctor.
